title: Sequenced on-prem request sifter and comm paths for air-gapped upgrades
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Create a deterministic intake and prioritization 'sifter' for private/VPC/on‑prem customer requests that involve networking changes, scheduled upgrades, and air‑gapped constraints. The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution for enterprise requests by providing a sequence of automated checks, human review gates, and standard communication paths (internal and customer-facing) so we can safely scope, schedule, and execute upgrades in regulated environments without overloading engineering or missing compliance steps.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Intake form captures network topology, upgrade tolerances, maintenance windows, and airgap constraints.
2) Automated preflight returns a risk score and required artifact checklist within 48 hours.
3) Triage lanes and SLA buckets (Emergency / High / Medium / Low) defined and aligned with Sales/CS/Support.
4) Playbook templates for customer comms and internal handoffs exist for each lane.
5) Integration tests with ENG preflight tooling (ENG-4412) and Scheduler (PM-20789) completed and demoed to SRE/Support.
decisions:
- Use a scored sifter rather than manual label-only triage to ensure consistent prioritization.
- Risk scoring will combine: network complexity (NAT/firewalls/egress restrictions), upgrade surface (agents, runtime, data-plane), and business criticality provided by CS.
- Maintain a 'fast-path' for urgent security upgrades with a 24–72 hour SLA if customer opts into paid expedited handling.
- Do not attempt to automate packaging for every air‑gapped customer; focus on preflight and documentation automation first.
tradeoffs:
- Automating preflight reduces manual work but may produce false positives; we will include a human override gate.
- Fast-path SLA reduces time-to-fix for critical customers but increases operational load; will be gated to paid customers and require runbook signoff.
- Building a universal airgap packager is high-cost; we prioritize templates and a validated checklist to cover 80% of requests.

risks:
- Under-specified customer inputs leading to rework and missed maintenance windows.
- Resource contention on ENG for preflight integration.
- Scope creep: customers requesting custom airgap packaging beyond templates.
- Regulatory approvals (e.g., crypto/KMS changes) may add multi-week delays unless pre-identified.
owner_notes: Prefer a phased rollout: Phase 1 (intake + scoring + templates), Phase 2 (automation hooks + fast-path SLA), Phase 3 (packaging assistance program). Coordinate with Growth for eligibility criteria for fast-path.
communication_plan: Internal: Weekly status to Eng Leads, SRE, Support, and Sales via the Private-Deploys channel. Customer: templated acknowledgement within 24h of intake, triage outcome within 48h, and scheduled upgrade plan within agreed SLA. Templates stored in Drive linked above.
metrics:
- Time-to-triage (hours)
- % of requests with complete intake on first submission
- Time-to-schedule for High/Medium/Low buckets
- Number of rollbacks post-upgrade
